posts.text: i just made my own personal website. eeshanagarwal.com feel free to comment any suggestions!

🥈i just won 2nd at the UofT School of Cities track at Hack the Valley 11! my team and i built Calmpost — a smart compost bin that actually knows what you’re throwing away. 📷 drop something in and a webcam + Gemini vision service identifies it in real time 📊 your drops get logged, charted, and tracked with streaks and rewards 📱 Flutter app ties it all together — ESP32 sensors, FastAPI backend, TimescaleDB shoutout to my cracked teammates Henry Cai, Kevin Hill, and Jayden Shin who lowk carried the

i just hit my first $1000 month from ugc two months ago i had no idea what ugc even was. posting content WILL get you opportunities you never even knew existed, and this is just the start. none of this happens without Kamil Gulman. he showed me how the whole thing actually works. if you aren't building your personal brand rn, you're falling behind. drop a comment if you want to know how to start.

quitting my job before school started was the best investment i've made. not losing the money, but gaining the time. i was working part-time through the summer while trying to build a quant strategy, grow an instagram, and actually prepare for engineering + ivey. something had to go. 3 weeks in and the extra hours are the only reason i'm keeping up. if you're holding onto something that's costing you more than money, drop it.

networking and putting yourself out there is the greatest thing you can do for yourself. how are you supposed to compete with the waterloo cs major who does math olympiads for fun? you dont. you stop trying to out-credential people you'll never out-credential and start being the person who actually shows up, reaches out, and builds relationships with people already where you want to be. credentials get you in the pool. people get you the job. stop optimizing your resume and go talk to someone.

118 followers. a month ago it was 0. and honestly the follower count matters less than what happened because of those followers. i made my first dollar online because of it. not a lot. but the feeling of someone paying you because of something you built - that's different. none of that required 10,000 followers. it required actually showing up. the hardest part wasn't the content. that the work would compound before the metric did. turns out: it does. if you're sitting on something worth sharing
